A deep, playful pause — premium sound baths in {{CITY}}

Sink into a curated sonic ritual led by {{FACILITATOR_NAME}}. Expect shimmering harmonics, warm light, and guided breathwork.

  • Venue: {{VENUE_NAME}}

See Upcoming Book a Session

What you’ll feel

Warm vibrations beneath you, a gentle wash of overtones, and a soft expansion behind the eyes — a sound map for deep rest.

  • Instruments today: crystal bowls, chimes, and a deep Tibetan gong.
  • Duration: 75 minutes (arrival + grounding included).
  • Intensity: intensive restorative layering.

Is a sound bath right for you?

Short checklist to help you decide — playful, grounded, and precise.

You're in if

  • You want deep relaxation without guided imagery.
  • You’re curious about vibration-based healing.
  • You're ready for a concentrated, premium experience.

Not recommended if

  • You’re in the first trimester of pregnancy (consult us).
  • You have implantable electronic devices (pacemakers) — discuss first.
  • Open untreated trauma — consider 1:1 before group work.

What to bring

  • Yoga mat, blanket, pillow or bolster.
  • Eye covering (sleep mask works) and water bottle.
  • Loose layers — you’ll cool down during savasana.

If in doubt, reach out: {{EMAIL}} — we’ll guide you to the right format (group, 1:1, or private series).

Session flow — the ritual roadmap

A clear sequence so you know what to expect in our intensive sound sessions.

  1. Arrival & grounding (10–15 min) — soft tea, settle in, intention setting.
  2. Breath & gentle movement (5–10 min) — guided to move energy and tune the nervous system.
  3. Main soundscape (40–50 min) — layered instruments: crystal, monochord, specific gong work — tailored dynamics.
  4. Transition & silent reflection (5–8 min) — allow integration; slow return to room.
  5. Closing circle (5–10 min) — share, grounding tips, micro-habits to extend the benefit.

Instruments we might use

Expect a rotating palette: crystal singing bowls, tuned chimes, Himalayan bowls, monochord resonance, and light tuning forks for fine-grain frequency work.

Small rituals to extend the session

Playful, premium micro-habits — easy to do and high-return.

  • Lie down, play a single singing bowl or hum softly. Rest. Repeat for three nights post-session.
  • 5 rounds of longer exhales — (inhale 4, hold 2, exhale 6) — helps anchor the nervous system after intense sound exposure.
  • Warm water with lemon within 30 minutes; gentle movement and grounding foods that evening.

Investment

Transparent pricing for group and private offerings. Intensive layering included.
